scenario_text: A viscous incompressible fluid in a long straight channel is subjected to a suddenly applied, constant streamwise pressure gradient. The cross-sectionally averaged velocity evolves from its initial value as fluid inertia competes with viscous resistance at the stationary walls. The baseline model represents the dominant fully developed laminar response and its relaxation toward a finite steady flow speed.

derivation_notes: The constant-pressure startup balance is refined by allowing the effective laminar hydraulic resistance to increase with instantaneous mean speed, so the opposing wall-drag process is multiplicatively modulated by (1 + nonlinear_drag_coefficient*U). change_summary: The assumption of exactly linear wall drag over the full startup range is relaxed to amplitude-dependent laminar resistance. As a result, dU_dt is no longer affine in U and stronger-forced trajectories show earlier saturation and stronger downward curvature.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The wall-drag rate is a constant independent of instantaneous flow amplitude across the admissible startup range.

response_change.parent_relation: The mean-flow acceleration is an affine function of U with one constant relaxation rate, so every startup trajectory approaches steady state with a single exponential timescale.
response_change.child_relation: The wall-drag process remains opposing and dissipative but its effective rate increases with flow magnitude, making dU_dt a nonlinear decreasing function of U rather than strictly affine.
response_change.observable_effect: Under the same pressure gradient and density, trajectories with larger intermediate U decelerate more strongly relative to the parent prediction, giving a faster late-stage approach and stronger downward curvature of dU_dt versus U than any single linear relaxation law.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model idealizes viscous wall resistance as exactly linear in mean speed over the full admissible startup range, omitting finite-amplitude corrections to hydraulic resistance that become visible before turbulence or compressibility are relevant.

evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Amplitude-dependent laminar hydraulic resistance, represented as a nonlinear increase of dissipative wall drag with mean velocity due to finite-speed corrections to the cross-sectionally averaged momentum balance.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to keep the same pressure-driven startup mechanism but replace the constant linear drag law with an amplitude-dependent laminar resistance. The parent target mapping uses a single shared relaxation rate: at fixed pressure_gradient_magnitude, fluid_density, and viscous_drag_rate, dU_dt decreases linearly with U and all trajectories differ only by one exponential timescale and steady level. Varying pressure_gradient_magnitude across trajectories while holding fluid and geometry fixed exposes a concrete limitation: a single parent parameter set predicts the same normalized startup shape for all forcing levels, whereas the refined mechanism predicts that stronger forcing drives U into a regime with extra drag, causing more downward curvature in dU_dt(U) and a lower-than-linear growth of steady speed with forcing. This contrast changes the scored target mapping itself because dU_dt at the same observed U differs from the parent affine relation. The effect is admissible when speeds become large enough for finite-amplitude resistance corrections to matter but still remain laminar, fully developed, and nonnegative. In weak forcing or early time, the correction is negligible and the parent is recovered.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.R: dimensionless resistance factor; startup-memory effects are observable when it evolves from 0 toward values of order 1 + nonlinear_drag_coefficient*U, typically remaining nonnegative in admissible laminar startup trajectories
new_symbol_range_suggestions.resistance_relaxation_rate: positive; memory is most observable when resistance_relaxation_rate / viscous_drag_rate is O(1), while resistance_relaxation_rate >> viscous_drag_rate approaches the parent quasistatic-drag limit

derivation_notes: The parent treats wall resistance as an instantaneous algebraic function of U. Here the same velocity-dependent laminar resistance target is retained, but a finite relaxation time is introduced for cross-sectional wall-shear establishment; the non-degenerate initial condition R = 0 represents minimal startup resistance and does not close the feedback branch because the imposed pressure gradient immediately drives U upward and then drives R away from zero.
change_summary: The instantaneous drag factor 1 + nonlinear_drag_coefficient*U is replaced by a lagged resistance state R that relaxes toward that finite target. This adds physically motivated startup memory and changes the curvature of the observed U(t) trajectory under the same constant pressure forcing.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The dissipative wall resistance is an instantaneous algebraic function of the current cross-sectionally averaged velocity.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Finite-time establishment of the wall-shear/hydraulic-resistance field during startup of internal flow, creating drag memory relative to the mean velocity.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: When resistance_relaxation_rate tends to infinity, R rapidly approaches 1 + nonlinear_drag_coefficient*U and the U equation reduces to the parent law.

response_change.parent_relation: The mean-velocity acceleration is an instantaneous function of U alone: dU_dt = constant drive minus a memoryless drag that grows monotonically with U, so startup trajectories approach steady state with one relaxation phase set by the current velocity.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same pressure-drive versus dissipative-drag balance, but relax the assumption that wall resistance adjusts instantaneously; introduce a finite-time hydrodynamic resistance buildup so dU_dt depends on both U and a lagged resistance state, changing the startup curvature even at the same U.
response_change.observable_effect: Under the same constant pressure gradient and zero initial mean velocity, the child can show weaker initial drag and then a delayed drag buildup, producing a more sharply bent startup trajectory and delayed approach to steady flow compared with the parent's single-phase relaxation.

evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the scored target no longer depends on U through a single algebraic branch; the additional state carries path-dependent resistance saturation toward a finite target, so trajectories with the same U can have different dU_dt depending on resistance history.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The dissipative wall resistance is an instantaneous algebraic function of the current cross-sectionally averaged velocity.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The wall-shear resistance approaches its velocity-dependent finite target with a nonzero relaxation time during startup.
evolution_contract.before_fragment: pressure_gradient_magnitude / fluid_density - viscous_drag_rate * (1 + nonlinear_drag_coefficient * U) * U

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes amplitude-dependent wall drag responds instantaneously to the current mean velocity, omitting transient development of the cross-sectional shear profile after sudden startup.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The dissipative wall resistance is an instantaneous algebraic function of the current cross-sectionally averaged velocity.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite-time establishment of the wall-shear/hydraulic-resistance field during startup of internal flow, creating drag memory relative to the mean velocity.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent maps the observed state U directly to dU_dt through a single-phase relaxation law: for fixed pressure_gradient_magnitude, fluid_density, viscous_drag_rate, and nonlinear_drag_coefficient, the acceleration at a given U is unique and independent of how recently the flow started. That is a realistic shortcut for rapid cross-sectional equilibration, but startup channel flow can exhibit delayed buildup of wall shear, especially when the shear-profile adjustment time is comparable to the mean-velocity evolution time. The scientifically relevant refinement is therefore to relax the instantaneous-drag assumption rather than adding an unrelated force. Varied condition: the dimensionless ratio of resistance-adjustment time to viscous-decay time, with the imposed pressure gradient held constant within each trajectory and geometry/fluid properties fixed. Observable contrast: two trajectories reaching similar U during startup can have different dU_dt because effective drag is still catching up in the child, whereas the parent forces the same dU_dt at that U. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. The effect is admissible when startup is observed soon after forcing onset and is strongest when forcing is large enough that nonlinear drag matters before drag memory has decayed. Limitation: if resistance adjustment is much faster than velocity evolution, the child collapses back to the parent and the extra state becomes unidentifiable.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the laminar resistance target increases only affinely with mean velocity, which is an overly rigid closure once finite-speed corrections make wall-drag growth stronger than linear over the admissible startup range.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The lagged hydraulic-resistance state relaxes toward the exact instantaneous target 1 + nonlinear_drag_coefficient*U.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Non-affine growth of laminar hydraulic resistance with mean velocity, representing higher-order finite-speed corrections to the cross-sectionally averaged wall-shear relation while preserving dissipative drag.
evolution_plan.rationale: Vary the imposed pressure-gradient magnitude across trajectories while holding fluid_density, viscous_drag_rate, resistance_relaxation_rate, and nonlinear_drag_coefficient fixed. In the parent, after accounting for lag through R, acceleration falls with U through an effectively single affine drag-growth law, so one shared parameter set imposes nearly the same dU_dt-versus-U curvature structure at all accessible speeds. A realistic next refinement is to relax that affine resistance-target assumption: at modest startup speeds the child remains close to the parent, but when nonlinear_drag_coefficient*U reaches order unity the resistance should increase faster than linearly, producing stronger downward curvature in the target mapping from observed (U,R) to dU_dt and a lower saturation speed. This changes the scored target relationship itself, not merely the auxiliary R trajectory, because dU_dt directly depends on the resistance level generated by the refined U-to-R target. The effect is admissible in laminar startup provided the added drag growth stays nonnegative and dissipative; it is weak near U=0, so the refinement is specifically justified only when sampled trajectories reach moderate speeds.

assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Setting startup_phase_coupling = 0 keeps H identically at 0 from its zero initial condition, so the added multiplicative relaxation enhancement vanishes and the parent ODE system is exactly recovered.

This is a genuine change to the target mapping because the altered kinetics of resistance states feed back into dU_dt, not merely into unscored auxiliary trajectories. The effect is scientifically admissible in laminar startup without violating positivity or finite steady speed, provided the added phase variable only increases dissipative drag establishment and decays away so the parent is recovered when that extra phase effect is removed.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Use a finite-capacity, saturation, threshold, or regime-transition response.

states.rhs: resistance_relaxation_rate * (1 + H) * ((1 + nonlinear_drag_coefficient * drag_saturation_velocity * tanh(U / drag_saturation_velocity)) - R)
states.description: Lagged dimensionless fast hydraulic-resistance state that relaxes toward a saturating non-affine laminar drag factor, with transient startup-phase-enhanced establishment rate

states.rhs: slow_resistance_relaxation_rate * (1 + H) * (tanh(1 + nonlinear_drag_coefficient * drag_saturation_velocity * tanh(U / drag_saturation_velocity)) - Q)
states.description: Lagged dimensionless slow wall-shear-memory resistance state with finite-capacity saturating buildup and transient startup-phase-enhanced establishment rate
Transient dimensionless startup wall-shear development phase that is populated by finite-speed startup intensity and decays as the flow profile develops

scenario_text: A viscous incompressible fluid in a long straight channel is subjected to a suddenly applied, constant streamwise pressure gradient. The cross-sectionally averaged velocity evolves from its initial value as fluid inertia competes with viscous resistance at the stationary walls. Geometry, fluid properties, and the imposed pressure gradient are fixed across trajectories, so the benchmark targets the instantaneous acceleration along each startup trajectory. The baseline model represents the dominant fully developed laminar response and its relaxation toward a finite steady flow speed.
promotion_reason: A new state is needed because the omitted effect is dynamic resistance-establishment hysteresis, not a static algebraic reshaping of the existing drag target. Existing U, R, and Q can represent current speed and two lagged drag levels, but they cannot separately encode whether the wall-shear profile is temporarily in a rapid-establishment versus slow-establishment phase under the same instantaneous U, R, and Q.

response_change.parent_relation: The scored acceleration is a pressure-driving constant minus a drag term linear in U, with all startup history entering only through drag buildup states R and Q. For fixed observed U, R, and Q, dU_dt decreases linearly with U and has no additional dependence on whether the flow is still accelerating strongly.
response_change.child_relation: Retain pressure driving and dissipative wall drag, but relax the assumption that the lagged resistance seen by the mean flow adjusts with a fixed relaxation rate. Let the hydraulic-resistance establishment rate itself depend on the current startup intensity so drag builds faster during strong acceleration/high-U startup and more slowly near equilibrium, feeding back into the scored dU_dt through altered resistance-state evolution.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with the same fixed parameters but different portions of startup, the child produces earlier bending-down of U(t) and a stronger mid-startup drop in dU_dt at moderate U than the parent's single-timescale resistance buildup, while recovering similar late-time behavior near steady flow.

diagnostic_groups.name: startup_intensity
diagnostic_groups.role: Dimensionless speed level indicating whether finite-speed startup corrections are active

diagnostic_groups.name: fast_drag_deficit
diagnostic_groups.role: Gap between instantaneous fast-resistance target and realized fast resistance

diagnostic_groups.name: slow_drag_deficit
diagnostic_groups.role: Gap between slow memory target and realized slow resistance

activation_condition: Observable when startup reaches moderate dimensionless speed |U|/drag_saturation_velocity = O(1) before R and Q have equilibrated, especially when resistance_relaxation_rate is not so large that drag is effectively instantaneous and not so small that all trajectories remain in an almost purely inertial regime over the observation window.
train_hidden_contrast: In training, this appears as extra downward curvature of dU_dt versus time and versus U during early-to-intermediate startup; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to trajectories where the pressure-driven rise reaches the nonlinear drag-growth scale faster or slower, shifting when the resistance field catches up without changing the constant forcing assumption.
continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the acceleration-dependent correction to the resistance-establishment law to zero, so the fast and slow resistance branches again relax with their original fixed rates.

dependent_variable.description: Time derivative of the cross-sectionally averaged streamwise fluid velocity

Lagged dimensionless slow wall-shear-memory resistance state contributing additional delayed drag
Dimensionless transient startup wall-shear development phase that boosts resistance-establishment rates during strong startup and decays as the profile develops

Constant fluid density

Positive velocity scale at which the resistance-growth correction transitions from affine to saturated stronger drag growth
Positive base relaxation rate of the added slow wall-shear-memory resistance branch
Positive dimensionless weight of the slow resistance contribution in the drag law
Positive decay rate of the transient startup phase state
